pundit.name: Landon Donovan
pundit.take:
I feel for "Ghost Pepper," I really do, but when you look at Devin drafting Haiti in the fourth round, you have to wonder if he thought he was picking an exotic fruit rather than a national team — bless his heart. Look, Devin's Spain got him 13 points yesterday, but that was more about Belgium's errors than his strategic genius. But I get it, he's in second place, with 71 points and only 10 behind "Bubba G," yet doesn't it seem like he's hanging on with duct tape and dreams? Going into the Norway vs. England match, it's almost endearing to think Devin believes Norway can overpower Gayden's England, the latter being essentially John Stones and a prayer. 

"The Backpass Assassin" has pulled off 39 points and clearly has a penchant for picking teams like Jordan that you'd expect to see playing five-a-side at the local rec center rather than on the world stage. Norway vs. England promises to be a clash of misplaced hopes, with Gayden basically betting the farm on Harry Kane's ability to outpace the Norwegian defense, which is a bit like betting on a tortoise in a 100m sprint. With England's recent form being as reassuring as a soggy tea bag, I absolutely guarantee England will navigate their way to a win, even if Gayden's team selections still look like he's checked out of a strategy meeting early. Ultimately, both managers mean well, but it's like watching two guys argue over who's got the prettiest rock in a mud pit.
